rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains qitmir as the thin membrane wrapped around a date pit; it represents the tiniest thing, underscoring that idols own nothing.
rows.anchor: كما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : لفافة النواة , وهي القشرة الرقيقة الملتفة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by interweaving the two denials: mention of ownership first signals its later omission, and the later mention signals the first omission.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الملك أولا دليلا على حذفه ثانيا , والملك ثانيا دليلا على حذفه أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether invoked in worship or for help, the inanimate objects cannot hear their worshippers at any time.
rows.anchor: أي المعبودات من دونه دعاء عبادة أو استغاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if they heard, they would not answer because they would know that granting the requests displeases God; they had refused the trust rather than act against His pleasure.
rows.anchor: لأنهم إذ ذاك يعملون أن إجابتكم لا ترضي الله , وهم مما أبى أن يحمل الأمانة ويخون فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, even granting hearing, it does not entail speech or the ability to fulfill a request; this reading includes living beings worshipped, since animals hear and answer while responders may lack the requested capacity.
rows.anchor: ولو فرض أنه يوجد لهم سمع , أو ولو كانوا سامعين - ليدخل فيه من عبد من الأحياء - ما لزم من السماع إجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God makes the objects speak on Judgment Day, they will deny the association people made with them and disown it.
rows.anchor: أي حين ينطقهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse turns away from those who neither admit nor properly understand or follow the warning, addressing instead someone capable of full understanding and obedience.
rows.anchor: صرف الخطاب عنهم إلى من له الفهم التام والطاعة الكاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one gives an account as authoritative as the all-knowing God; His report cannot be challenged, while other reports invite criticism.
rows.anchor: أي بالغ الخبر , فلا يمكن الطعن في شيء مما أخبر به , وأما غيره فلا يخبر خبرا إلا يوجه إليه نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people are dependent on God: their extensive knowledge, thought, and intellect multiply their competing needs, while their weakness and incapacity make other creatures' need seem negligible.
rows.anchor: لاتساع معارفكم وسريان أفكاركم وانتشار عقولكم تكثر نوازغكم وتتفرق دواعيكم فيعظم احتياجكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite predicate al-fuqarāʾ conveys this particular, encompassing poverty; an indefinite predicate would not express the same force.
rows.anchor: ولو نكر الخبر لم يفد هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri distinguishes universal created poverty, dependence on God to originate and sustain, from poverty as detachment; commoners detach from wealth, the elect from causes, and true praiseworthy poverty is detachment of the heart from effects.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : والفقر على ضربين : فقر خلقة , وفقر صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is absolutely self-sufficient: He needs neither people, their worship, nor anything whatsoever.
rows.anchor: أي الذي لا يتصور أن يحتاج لا إليكم ولا إلى عبادتكم ولا إلى شيء أصلا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines praise as the perfection of a whole when every part and matter reaches its full end; a deficient part prevents the whole from being wholly praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: وكان الحمد كما قال الحرالي في شرح الأسماء : حسن الكلية بانتهاء كل أمر وجزء , وبعض منها إلى غاية تمامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates everything fittingly and at its appointed measure, without haste; blame arises from viewing parts in isolation rather than seeing the whole.
rows.anchor: وكان الله قد خلق كل شيء كما ينبغي , لم يعجل شيئا عن إناه وقدره , وكان الذم استنقاضا يلحق بعض الأجزاء

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali defines a praiseworthy human as one whose habits, character, and deeds are all praised without exception.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال الغزالي : الحميد من العباد من حمدت عوائده وأخلاقه وأعماله كلها من غير مثنوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike created wealth, which cannot satisfy all who seek it and is constrained by fear or other limits, God's gifts are unrestricted and His praise is complete.
rows.anchor: الغنى من الخلق لا يسع غناه من يقصده , وإن وسعهم لم يسعهم عطاؤه لخوف الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has poured out visible and hidden blessings and enabled people to receive them; His gifts are not barred, as the cited verse says.
rows.anchor: أسبغها ظاهرة وباطنة , وجعل لهم قدرة على تناولها . لا يعوق عنه إلا قدرته ( وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's giving and withholding are both praiseworthy: neither serves a self-interested aim, but follows wisdom too subtle for minds to grasp.
rows.anchor: كان إعطاؤه حمدا ومنعه حمدا , لأنه لا يكون مانعا لغرض بل لحكمة تدق عن الأفكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can remove all people and bring another creation in their place; He is able to do so without difficulty and is praised in annihilation as in creation.
rows.anchor: غيركم لأنه على كل شيء قدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent two messengers so each could support the other and strengthen their mission; they announced that they had been sent to call the people to faith in God.
rows.anchor: ليعضد أحدهما الآخر فيكون أشد لأمرهما فأخبراهم بإرسالها إليهم كأن قالا : نحن رسولان إليكم لتؤمنوا بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople denied the messengers despite their signs; God sends no messenger without signs of the kind by which people may believe, directly or through another messenger.
rows.anchor: لأنه من المعلوم أنا ما أرسلنا رسولا إلا كان معه من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر

rows.speaker: طفيل بن عمرو الدوسي
rows.claim: As an example of a sign requested from the Prophet, Tufayl ibn Amr al-Dawsi received a light on his forehead and, after asking, on his whip instead.
rows.anchor: كما كان للطفيل بن عمرو الدوسي ذي النور لما ذهب إلى قومه وسأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن تكون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzzaznā means that God brought might, strength, and victory to His cause or His messenger after the messengers were weakened by denial.
rows.anchor: فأوقعنا العزة , وهي القوة والشدة والغلبة , لأمرنا أو لرسولنا

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from ʿAsim reads ʿazaznā with a lightened consonant, supporting the sense of bringing victory or might.
rows.anchor: بما أشارت إليه قراءة أبي بكر عن عاصم بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a third messenger with the same commission as the first two, and the three reiterated that they had been sent specifically to this people.
rows.anchor: أرسلناه بما أرسلناهما به

rows.speaker: أهل القرية
rows.claim: The townspeople argue that the messengers are merely human like themselves and ask what qualifies them, rather than the townspeople, for messengership.
rows.anchor: أي أهل القرية : { ما أنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the exceptive particle cancels the negation in mā antum illā, the phrase after illā is raised as the negation's syntactic governance falls away.
rows.anchor: زال عملها فارتفع قوله : { بشرمثلنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains their argument: the All-Merciful's universal mercy and their equal servitude should mean He gives them the same status, not privileging the messengers.
rows.anchor: فعموم رحمته مع استوائنا في عبوديته تقتضي أن يسوي بيننا في الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads the townspeople as emphatically insisting that the messengers are liars in both their present claim and its future outcome.
rows.anchor: قالوا دافعين لذلك : { إن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers answer that their Lord knows their commission, as shown by the signs He produces through them and His protection from their opponents' plots.
rows.anchor: ولذلك يظهر على أيدينا الآيات , ويحمينا ممن يكيدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appeal to God's knowledge functions like an oath, as does the expression 'God bears witness.'
rows.anchor: وهذه العبارة تجري مجرى القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first declaration began the message; the repeated, emphatic declarations answer the people's denial, with each formulation tailored to its place in the exchange.
rows.anchor: فالأول ابتداء أخبار , وهذان جوابا إنكار , فأعطى كلا ما يستحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers owe only clear delivery on behalf of God, supported by decisive verbal and practical proofs, including miracles; their sender's knowledge and signs testify for them.
rows.anchor: أي المؤيد بالأدلة القطعية من الحجج القولية والفعلية بالمعجزات وغيرها , فلولا أنه يعلم لما أمكننا شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people's gods cannot clarify anything about themselves because they lack knowledge, unlike the messengers' knowledgeable sender who bears witness to their mission.
rows.anchor: كما أن آلهتكم لما لم يكن لها علم لم يقدروا على بيان في أمرها بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrival of righteous people among a community can be a blessing or a punishment according to whether people believe and act well; these deniers faced drought, hardship, and other trials.
rows.anchor: حلول الصالحين بين الناس يكون تارة نعمة وأخرى نقمة باعتبار التصديق والتكذيب والإساءة والإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople say they deliberately and conspicuously took the messengers as a bad omen, blaming their misfortune on them; this explicit wording differs from expressions in al-Naml and al-Aʿraf.
rows.anchor: أي حملنا أنفسنا على الطيرة والتشاوم تطيرا ظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ignorant custom is to call what they favor auspicious and credit its blessings to good fortune, then blame disliked events on the ill omen of others.
rows.anchor: عادة الجهال التيمن بما مالوا إليه ويسندون ما حل بهم من نعمة إلى يمنة والتشاوم بما كرهوه

rows.speaker: أهل القرية
rows.claim: They demand that the messengers stop their summons, and insist under oath that they will not relent in their threat.
rows.anchor: أي عن دعائكم هذا { لنرجمنكم } أي لنشتمنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajm here may mean cursing or insulting, pelting with stones until they stop, or killing them brutally.
rows.anchor: أي لنشتمنكم أو لنرمينكم بالحجارة حتى تنتهوا أو لنقتلنكم شر قتلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat promises that punishment will come from the townspeople themselves, emphasizing that they will personally inflict it.
rows.anchor: أي عاجلا لا من غيرنا كما تقولون أنتم في تهديدكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the choice of 'touch' over 'contact' by noting that a person may act without the intended effect taking hold.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان قد يفعل ما لا يؤخذ أثره فقالوا معبرين بالمس دون الإمساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers answer that the people's ill fortune is with them: it is their own evil conduct, including their denial, that brings the trial.
rows.anchor: أي شومكم الذي أحل لكم البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the earlier proof that God changes a person from one condition to another, and the affirmation of His encompassing knowledge, the text gives a clearer argument for resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولما أثبت سبحانه بهذا الدليل قدرته على ما هدد به أولا من التحويل من حال إلى أخرى , فثبتت بذلك قدرته على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here seeing means knowing with a certainty and obviousness comparable to seeing with one's eyes.
rows.anchor: أي يعلم علما هو في ظهوره كالمحسوس بالبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān denotes the human species, including this particular opponent and others, although one individual was the occasion for the verse.
rows.anchor: أي جنسه منهم ومن غيرهم وإن كان الذي نزلت فيه واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity began as a tiny, contemptible drop of water with no use, while God had created the human's father from soil and mother from flesh and bones.
rows.anchor: شيء يسير حقير من ماء لا انتفاع به بعد إبداعنا أباه من تراب وأمه من لحم وعظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden turn from a lowly origin to an articulate adversary is astonishing: the human uses God-given reason, power, and speech to dispute God's messengers and people dear to Him.
rows.anchor: من أعطاء العقل والقدرة في قدرته

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri quotes a poem illustrating how a pupil trained in archery turns his skill against his teacher once strong.
rows.anchor: أنشد الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري في ذلك : أعلمه الرماية كل يوم فلما اشتد ساعدوه رماني

rows.speaker: أبي بن خلف الجمحي
rows.claim: The occasion was Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, whom the Prophet killed in single combat at Uhud; he is the primary target of this rebuke.
rows.anchor: وسبب النزول أبي بن خلف الجمحي الذي قتله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأحد مبارزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponent makes the powerless idols he worships a comparison for God, despite reason showing that nothing resembles the Creator and idols can do nothing.
rows.anchor: أي آلهته التي عبدها لكونها لا تقدر على شيء مكابرا لعقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasiya khalqahu can mean that he became heedless of his creation or that he abandoned reflection on it.
rows.anchor: والنسيان هنا يحتمل أن يكون بمعنى الذهول , وأن بكون بمعنى الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy is so foolish that it would not satisfy even a donkey if one could speak, rebuking the opponent's obtuseness.
rows.anchor: هذا المثل الذب قاله هذا الكافر لا يرضاه حمار لو نطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question treats reviving the dead as impossible; bones are the hardest matter and least receptive to life, especially once decayed and crumbled.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت العظام أصلب شيء وأبعده عن قبول الحياة لا سيما إذا بليت وأرفتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramīm means the bones have become dust that is carried along by the wind.
rows.anchor: أي صارت ترابا يمر مع الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because listeners await a reply to the objection, the command to speak begins the answer and addresses the person able to understand the dispute fully.
rows.anchor: ولما كان موطنا يتشوف فيه السامع لهذا الكلام إلى جوابه , استأنف قوله مخاطبا من لا يفهم هذه المجادلة حق فهمها غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer repeats the verb 'revive' explicitly to prevent evasive argument and to stress the intended point.
rows.anchor: وأعاد فعل الإحياء نصا على المراد دفعا للتعنت ودلالة على الاهتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who originated the bones from nothing and gave them life the first time can restore them a second time; original creation proves the ability to recreate.
rows.anchor: أي فإن كل من قدر على إيجاد شيء أول مرة فهو قادر على إعادته ثاني مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because life can enter bone, bone becomes impure at death; the verse therefore supports the ruling that a dead animal's bones are impure.
rows.anchor: وهي شاهدة بأن الحياة تحل العظم فيتنجس بالموت مما يحكم بنجاسة ميتته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalq here means every possible act of making and measuring, whether bringing something into being initially or recreating it.
rows.anchor: أي صنع وتقدير ممكن أن يخلق من ذلك ومن غيره ابتداء وإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every particle of a dead person even if scattered across land and sea, as well as everything else.
rows.anchor: فلا يخفى عليه أجراء ميت أصلا وإن تفرقت في البر والبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a case of badīʿ al-iḥtibāk: first resurrection points to the second, second origination to the first, and 'first time' implies a second time.
rows.anchor: فالآية من بديع الاحتباك : الإحياء أولا دال على مثله ثانيا , والإنشاء ثانيا دال على مثله أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof completes the surah's prior descriptions of resurrection, gathering, judgment, and the afterlife, together establishing bodily and spiritual resurrection.
rows.anchor: فقد بلغ هذا البيان في الدلالة على البعث الجسماني والروحاني معا النهاية التي ليش وراءها بيان

words: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلْأَخْضَرِ نَارًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To recall God's perfection and prompt submission, the verse points to His extracting the most hidden thing, fire, from its opposite, green wood containing visible water.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على التذكير بالموصوف ليستحضر ما له من صفات الكمال فيبادر إلى الخضوع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People make fire by rubbing two green, water-dripping sticks together: al-murkh, described as male, against al-ʿafār, described as female.
rows.anchor: فيَسحق المرخ - وهو ذكر - على العفار - وهو أنثى - فتخرج النار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan transmits Ibn Abbas's report that every tree contains fire except the ʿunāb tree.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ليس شجر إلا وفيه نار إلا العناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's aim is to show that God's army ultimately prevails, even when apparently weak and victory is delayed, and that the ending brings safety to both sides, as promised at the end of al-Saffat.
rows.anchor: بيان ما ذكر في آخر الصافات من أن جند الله هم الغالبون - وإن رئي أنهم ضعفاء ، وإن تأخر نصرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's oneness follows from His encompassing all attributes of perfection, as the end of al-Saffat indicates through glorification, praise, and related themes.
rows.anchor: لأنه سبحانه واحد لكونه محيطا بصفات الكمال كما أفهمه آخر الصافات من التنزيه والحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter ṣād is articulated at the tongue's tip against the lower incisors and has the qualities of breathiness, softness, closure, elevation, and whistling; its strong, numerous qualities suit the surah's theme of prevailing might.
rows.anchor: لأن مخرجه من طرف اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter's articulation is especially accessible, open, light, agile, and dominant, while its elevated qualities exceed their opposites in force and grandeur.
rows.anchor: لأن مخرجه أمكن مخارج الحروف وأوسعها وأخفها وأرشقها وأغلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah mentions prophets who did not destroy their opponents but were tested and then protected by God from enemies among jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: ولذلك ذكر من فيها من الأنبياء الذين لم يكن على أيديهم إهلاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وآخرون
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others interpret ṣād as saying that God is truthful in His promise, that Muhammad is truthful, or that Muhammad has captured and drawn people's hearts.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وعن غيره من أن معناه

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr has a rare reading of ṣād as a past-tense verb from the root for hunting, meaning that Muhammad captured hearts.
rows.anchor: وبه قرأ أبو عمرو في رواية شاذة على أنه فعل ماض من الصيد

rows.speaker: الحسن وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and others read ṣād with kasra as an imperative from muṣādāh, challenging the Prophet to confront people with revelation and prevail through truth.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وغيره بكسر الصاد على أنه أمر من المصاداة وهي المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth is God's sword on earth: wherever it is placed it cuts through, and the revelation's truth draws everyone who has any share of truth.
rows.anchor: لأن الصدق سيف الله في أرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the scholars of God, ṣād points to truth as correspondence between creation and the divine command; the prophets are living witnesses to this meaning.
rows.anchor: معنى الصاد عند العلماء الربانيين من أنه مطابقة ما بين الخلق والأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of truth leads to the following surah, which praises the one who brought truth and affirmed it.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال في السورة التي بعدها

rows.speaker: ابن الجوزي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi calls this the sūra of David.
rows.anchor: وتسمى سورة داود عليه السلام - كما قاله ابن الجوزي رحمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's course best exemplifies the surah's aim among its prophets: he began in weakness and ended with kingship.
rows.anchor: وحاله صلى الله عليه وسلم أدل أحوال من فيها من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala invokes God who strengthens those attached to Him despite weakness, the Merciful who can show mercy in hardship as in ease, and the Compassionate who helps His beloved persist in gratitude.
rows.anchor: الذي يعز من انتمى إليه وإن كان ضعيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After al-Saffat ends by declaring God's perfection and might and the messengers' safety, this surah opens by showing the defeat of those who dispute that truth.
rows.anchor: ولما نزه ربنا سبحانه نفسه الأقدس في ختام تلك عن كل شائبة نقص , وأثبت له كل كمال ناصا على العزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening letter signals that the Prophet, though presently weak, is commissioned to challenge the disobedient and has been promised victory that will spread widely.
rows.anchor: إما أمرك - يا من أمرناه باستفتاء العصاة آخر الصافات وبشرناه بالنصر - مهيأ مع الضعف الذي أنتم به الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran gathers clear explanation of every good and has immeasurably many followers, beyond any count or limit.
rows.anchor: الجامع - مع البيان لكل خير - لأتباع لا يحصيهم العد , ولا يحيط بهم الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath suits only something the one addressed recognizes as exalted; the Quran is reminder, admonition, honor, and truth no one can doubt, destined to fill the lands and surpass every measure.
rows.anchor: ولما كان القسم لا يليث ولا يحسن إلا بما يعتقد المقسم له شرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although disbelievers publicly voice doubt and disparage the Quran, inwardly they know its truth and greatness.
rows.anchor: والذين كفروا وإن أظهروا الشك في ذلك وانتقصوه قولا فإنهم لا ينتقصونه علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIzza means difficulty, stubbornness, and competitive pride rooted in pagan zeal; enclosed in it, the disbelievers are blinded to truth.
rows.anchor: أي عسر وصعوبة ومغالبة بحمية الجاهلية مظروفون لها , فهي معمية لهم عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine form signals the pride's weakness and promises its swift disappearance and reversal into humiliation.
rows.anchor: وأنثها إشارة إلى ضعفها , وبشارة بسرعة زوالها وانقلابها إلى ذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shiqāq is turning away, refusing, and arrogantly rejecting the truth conveyed by the signs of existence and the Quran's words.
rows.anchor: أي إعراض وامتناع واستكبار على قبول الصدق من لساني الحال الذي أفصح به الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation guides people toward what their nature already contains through the clearest expression, but they turn away in defiance rather than conviction; the unjust reject God's signs.
rows.anchor: فأعرضوا عن تدبره عنادا منهم لا اعتقادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two nouns are indefinite to magnify the pride and opposition.
rows.anchor: وتنكيرهما للتعظيم

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the answer to the oath is omitted so the mind can range widely, making its meaning richer and more expansive.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : حذف الجواب ليذهب فيه القلب كل مذهب ليكون أغزر وبحوره أزخر

words: كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the account of earlier peoples' rebellion and punishment to the Arab polytheists, who repeat the same offense and deserve the same punishment.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما ذكر تعالى حال الأمم السالفة مع أنبيائهم في العتو والتكذيب

words: كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The account of earlier punishment prepares for the next reminder of the polytheists' demand to hasten their share before Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: بذكر استعجالهم في قوله

words: كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The Prophet is then told to endure their speech and is comforted through accounts of earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: أتبع ذلك بأمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God discloses truth both through the created world and through speech; revelation is the clearer account, and rejecting it makes the arrogant liable to destruction, as shown in the following account of ruined warners.
rows.anchor: فأما الحال فهو ما تنطق به أحوال الموجودات التي أبدعها سبحانه في هذا الكون من علوم
